T: Eight legs, two fangs and an attitude.
D: A city doctor with a fear of spiders moves his family to a country town just as a deadly spider from Venezuela starts a colony in his barn.
P: Pour the red when Ross falls through the floor into his wine cellar.
S: Cornmeal arepas filled with black beans and cheese. It came from a tepui in Venezuela.

Mix the masarepa with the warm water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and rest for 5 minutes. Fry the onion, garlic and cumin in the oil, add the beans and a splash of water and mash roughly. Shape the dough into 8 small patties and cook on an oiled griddle until crusted on both sides. Split the arepas and stuff with beans, cheese, avocado and a squeeze of lime.
Devilled eggs with paprika. Ross gets nicknamed Doctor Death.

Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel. Halve them, mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar and half the paprika and season well. Pipe the yolk back into the whites. Dust with the rest of the paprika and top with fried shallots and chives.
M: Chicken and vegetable pot pie. Dr Metcalf won't retire yet.

Brown the chicken in half the butter and set aside. Soften the leeks, carrots and celery in the rest of the butter, then stir in the flour for a minute. Whisk in the stock and cream, add the chicken and thyme and simmer until thick, then stir in the peas. Spoon into a pie dish, lay the pastry over, crimp the edges, brush with egg and cut a steam hole. Bake at 200C until the pastry is puffed and deep golden.
Fish and shellfish stewed in tomato with fennel. They left the city for this.

Soften the onion, fennel and garlic in the oil with the chilli. Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer until rich. Add the fish and mussels, cover for 3 minutes, then add the prawns until pink and the mussels open. Scatter with parsley and serve with thick slices of grilled sourdough.
400g firm white fish fillets, in chunks@Seafood
W: Dark chocolate tart under a spun sugar web. Ross takes on the general in the cellar.

Line a 22cm tart tin with the pastry, fill with baking paper and rice and blind bake at 190C, then bake uncovered until golden. Bring the cream to a simmer, pour it over the chocolate and butter, stir until glossy and add the salt. Pour into the cooled case and chill until set. Melt the sugar in a dry pan to a pale caramel, then flick thin threads from a fork over a rolling pin to make a web. Lay the sugar web over the tart just before serving.
K: He throws his good wine at the spider.
Stir the wine, brandy, sugar and fruit together in a jug and chill. Add ice and soda water and pour.
